errors.english: the very occurrence of a conception of an entity cuts off the continuum of the conception of non-entity
errors.why: The instrumental བློས marks the cognition of non-entity as what cuts the continuum (of the arising cognition of entity), not the reverse.

note: Generally faithful rendering of a dense apoha/vāsanā argument; two unmarked explanatory glosses are run into the text but do not distort it.

errors.english: because that which causes destruction does not abide, owing to its own abidance
errors.why: The reason is that when the destroyer is absent the perishing thing abides by itself, so a separate cause of abiding is pointless; the English attributes the abiding to the destroyer and garbles the argument.

fix.find: because that which causes destruction does not abide, owing to its own abidance
fix.replace: because, when the destroyer is not present, the thing abides of itself

errors.english: the connecting mental consciousness itself is the sentient agent
errors.why: མཚམས་སྦྱོར་བ is pratisandhi, the rebirth-linking mental consciousness, and སེམས་དཔའ here is the being (sattva), not an 'agent'.

note: Mostly followable, but the opening dilemma on the cause of abiding is mistranslated and the rebirth-linking term is lost.

errors.why: The continuum transformed is that of the mantra (its successive moments acquiring distinctions); 'mental' is not in the Tibetan and shifts the referent.
དམངས་རིགས is the śūdra varṇa, contrasted with the brahmin; 'commoner' blurs the caste term.

errors.english: just as universals and manifestations cannot be
errors.why: སྤྱི་གསལ་[བ་དཔྱོད་པའི་སྐབས་སུ་བཤད་ཟིན] refers back to the section examining universals and manifestation where this was already explained, not a comparison.

note: Sound rendering of the Mīmāṃsā mantra-efficacy debate with a few referential slips.

errors.english: He clearly demonstrates the meanings of logical grounds.
errors.why: As the commentary parses it (next side: གཏན་ཚིགས་གསལ་བ ... དེས་དོན་སྟོན་པ), the verse means he shows the meanings by means of clear reasons, not 'the meanings of reasons'.

note: Faithful handling of the word-by-word compound analysis of the Jātakamālā verse.

errors.english: Remoteness in the case of inference is merely the opposite of subtlety of nature.
errors.why: The Tibetan says NON-remoteness (མ་བསྐལ་བ) for inference is merely the opposite of subtle nature.

fix.find: Remoteness in the case of inference
fix.replace: Non-remoteness in the case of inference

note: Careful and accurate on the observation/non-observation and substance/quality typology apart from one lost negation.
Accurate rendering of the Nyāyabindu commentary on the incomplete and unestablished pseudo-reasons, including the Digambara tree example.

errors.english: but they do not cease to belong to the category of reasons in that sense
errors.why: The argument is that deviating similar/dissimilar statements are pseudo-reasons and do not fall back into reason-hood, since the general rule has no scope where the exception applies; the English says they remain reasons.

note: Verses and prose of Dignāga's argument are well segmented; one clause in the general-rule/exception reply is inverted.
Faithful rendering of the commentary on the three-times analysis of mind and the plantain-tree simile.

errors.english: If they cover it with leaves, there is no offense.
errors.why: སྤང་ལེབ are slabs of turf/sod, not leaves.

note: Accurate Vinaya rendering of the pāyattika on building beyond three courses, with correct handling of the factors and the Questions citation.
Faithful rendering of the Sadāprarudita/Dharmodgata narrative as abridged in the commentary.
